system.name: NotebookOS
system.one_liner: a GPU-efficient replicated notebook platform that allocates GPUs only during active cell execution using Raft-synchronized kernel replicas

components.name: External Clients
components.role: notebook clients (Jupyter Notebook, Golang/JS/Python clients) submitting code for execution

components.name: Jupyter Server
components.role: receives client requests and forwards them via a Provisioner

components.name: Provisioner
components.role: customized Kernel Provisioner integrating NotebookOS with Jupyter

components.name: Global Scheduler
components.role: identifies candidate GPU servers, forwards/launches replicas, and migrates them under load

components.name: Local Scheduler
components.role: per-server scheduler managing kernel replicas on that GPU server

components.name: Standby Kernel Replica
components.role: non-executing replica that stays synchronized via Raft and can take over

components.name: Executor Kernel Replica
components.role: the replica actively executing code and dynamically bound to GPUs

components.name: AST
components.role: abstract syntax tree representation of executed code used for state synchronization

components.name: GPUs
components.role: GPU devices dynamically bound to the executor replica during active execution

components.name: Distributed Data Store
components.role: checkpoints large objects/GPU state outside the Raft log (AWS S3, HDFS, or Redis)

flows.what: run cell / submit code for execution

content.key_idea: NotebookOS routes each client request through a Global Scheduler to Local Schedulers on GPU servers, where one kernel replica executes with dynamically bound GPUs while standby replicas stay synchronized via Raft, and large state is offloaded to a distributed data store instead of the Raft log.
content.reading_order: Left to right, numbered steps 1-7: External Clients through Jupyter Server/Provisioner (1), to Global Scheduler (2-3), out to three Local Scheduler groups each with Standby/Executor replicas (4-6), and up to the Distributed Data Store (7) with the Executor's dynamic GPU binding and 1-kernel-composed-of-3-replicas bracket on the right.

summary: This figure gives the architecture overview of NotebookOS. External Clients (Jupyter, Golang, JS, Python) submit run-cell requests to the Jupyter Server's Provisioner (step 1), which forwards them to a Global Scheduler (step 2) that launches or migrates kernel replicas across GPU servers via per-server Local Schedulers (step 3). Each Local Scheduler manages a Distributed Kernel composed of one Executor Kernel Replica, which dynamically binds GPUs only during active execution (step 6) and represents code as an AST, and two Standby Kernel Replicas that stay synchronized with it via Raft (step 5). Large objects and GPU state are checkpointed asynchronously to an external Distributed Data Store (S3/HDFS/Redis, step 7) rather than the Raft log itself. Drawn as a dense, numbered hub-and-spoke diagram with a legend distinguishing allocated versus unallocated GPU icons, the figure walks the reader through NotebookOS's full request-to-execution-to-replication path.
summary_zh: 该图展示 NotebookOS 的整体架构：外部客户端请求经 Jupyter Server/Provisioner 转发给 Global Scheduler，再分发到各 GPU 服务器上的 Local Scheduler；每个分布式内核由一个动态绑定 GPU 的 Executor 副本和多个通过 Raft 同步的 Standby 副本组成，大对象/GPU 状态异步 checkpoint 到分布式数据存储，图中以编号步骤 1-7 串联整个流程。
